events.credibility_reason: Known only second-hand through a MathWorld citation of private correspondence, which MathWorld flags as possibly outdated.

Unidentified author on a non-reviewing preprint server; claims the primality of c5 (far beyond any known method) and from it the infinitude of Mersenne primes, a non sequitur; key lemma reportedly inverted; no engagement in about 29 months while c5 is still listed as of unknown primality.

why: The statement needs one unconditionally composite Catalan–Mersenne number, and no event provides one. The W(c4) factor (2020 curio, 2024 OEIS comment) makes c5 composite only if the open New Mersenne conjecture holds. That is a reduction to an unproven condition, so it scores none. I rejected the researcher's competing conditional reading for this reason. The trial-factoring bounds on c5 are finite searches (instances). Even if true, the May 2024 claim that c5 is prime would not decide the existence question, so it scores none. It is also not credible because several F10 signals appear together. Robinson 1954 and Dutta–Borah are about different claims (variant). Wagstaff and Baker do not address the iterated sequence. Baker's ChatGPT use was proofreading only, so its AI role is none.
doubts: The hyperbolic preprint was never opened; its content comes from search excerpts. The AlphaEvolve 67-problem list was not checked for a c_n item. The 54-digit factor was not verified, but this does not affect any answer.
